questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to apply advanced security controls to real-world CI/CD supply chains in multi-tenant environments, with emphasis on provenance verification, code signing, and rapid incident response.

## Key Concepts

- Software supply chain integrity
- Module provenance and signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Pre-merge and runtime policy enforcement (OPA/Conftest)
- Drift detection and automated remediation
- Incident response planning and execution

## Code Example

```rego
package ci.supplychain
default allow = false

allow {
    input.provenance.verified
    input.provenance.signer == "trusted-module-owner"
    input.provenance.entry_point == "main.tf"
    not input.provenance.dependencies[_].untrusted
}

deny[msg] {
    not allow
    msg := "Module provenance verification failed"
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical security controls for serverless applications and secrets management at a beginner level, focusing on tangible implementation steps and measurable success criteria.

## Key Concepts
- **Least-privilege IAM roles**: Grant only the permissions required for each Lambda function to operate
- **Secrets management with KMS/Secrets Manager**: Centralize sensitive data storage with encryption at rest
- **CI gate for secrets detection**: Prevent credential leakage by blocking secrets before they enter the codebase
- **Incident response workflow**: Structured 24-hour response playbook covering containment, investigation, eradication, and recovery
- **Audit and monitoring**: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and Lambda logging for visibility into function behavior

## Success Criteria
- All Lambda functions operate with custom IAM roles containing only necessary permissions
- Zero plaintext secrets in environment variables or codebase
- Secrets rotate automatically per defined schedule
- CI pipeline blocks all commits containing detected secrets
- Incident response playbook is documented, tested quarterly, and accessible to on-call personnel

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design multi-tenant token governance and rapid incident response across mobile/web apps, focusing on real-world controls (aud/iss checks, PKCE, device attestation, mTLS, OPA) rather than generic concepts.

- OAuth2/OIDC token binding and audience validation
- PKCE, short-lived tokens, and device-bound refresh tokens
- Token introspection at API gateways
- Per-tenant isolation in gateways/meshes (mTLS)
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) for runtime enforcement
- CI security gates and IR playbooks

## Code Example

```javascript
// validate token audience and issuer before granting access
function validateToken(token, expectedAud) {
  const { payload } = decodeJwt(token); // pseudo decoding
  if (payload.aud !== expectedAud) throw new Error('Invalid audience');
  if (payload.iss !== 'https://id.example.com') throw new Error('Invalid issuer');
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test tenant isolation in CI/CD and runtime? 
- What telemetry signals indicate token misuse across tenants?
